newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks move up on interest rate talk.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks move up on interest rate talk.

text.p: Prices on Cyprus's stock exchange gained 1.56 percent during a week marked by increased investor activity sparked by talk of a reduction in interest rates.
The CSE index, set at 100 points, closed at 76.99 on Friday, gaining 1.19 points from last week's close.

"The pessimistic climate prevailing in the first 1.5 months of this year was suceeded this week by moderate optimism as the publicity on the political front was toned down," said CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation in its weekly stock market review.

A climate of what leading businessmen have described as "artificial" tension was created early last month after disclosures Cyprus was buying an anti-aircraft system from Russia, and warnings from Turkey it would block the deployment of the missiles.
CISCO said that investors have shown increased interest in anticipation of the reduction in interest rates by half a percentage point.

A date has not been announced for the reduction, though media reports have suggested the island's central bank could recommend a reduction come into effect from March 1. The lending rate is currently 8.5 percent, and the deposit rate 7.0.

Banking stocks closed at 87.73, gaining 2.04 percent from its close last week. The closing price for Bank of Cyprus fully paid shares was 327.5 cents, gaining one cent during Friday's trading and six over the week.

Earlier in the day the bank announced net profit gains in 1996 of 5.4 percent. The bank, whose profits rose a record 30 percent in 1995, reported net profits of 24.2 million Cyprus pounds compared with 23 million in 1995.
Popular Bank,, which is due to announce its own preliminary 1996 results in a week's time, closed on its fully paid shares at 316, up five cents from Friday's close.
The Hellenic Bank gained 10 cents, closing at 267, while the Universal Savings Bank closed at 167.5 from 157.5 last week.
Universal Life Insurance dropped half a cent, closing at 402.5. Paneuropean closed at 107.5, while Interamerican Insurance closed at 99 cents from 95.5 last week.
Vassiliko Cement was up 2.5 cents, closing at 138.5, while beer and wine manufacturer Keo was trading at 103, down half a cent from last week.
Retailers Woolworth was trading at 77 cents, gaining half a cent.
